page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical ARM Neoverse-N2 cores operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz, complemented by 128 MB of L3 cache. The system provides 128.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no GPU acceleration hardware and features no local ephemeral storage, directing all disk I/O operations through attached network-based storage volumes.

Benchmark evaluation highlights an exceptionally capable memory subsystem, reaching uncached read speeds of 450.97 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 188.48 GB/sec, placing it within the top 10% tier. Multi-core computational output is strong, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19998.0 and Clang compilation score of 40208.0. In contrast, single-core execution metrics and vector throughput align with median cloud performance levels. PassMark database tests achieve top-tier ratings, while LLM inference throughput degrades considerably on large parameter models.

Without local disks or hardware accelerators bundled into the profile, the instance focuses compute cost efficiency on pure multi-threaded central processing and memory bandwidth. It is well-fitted for distributed database clusters, containerized application runtimes, continuous integration build agents, and high-throughput static web servers.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture, featuring 32 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.4 GHz and 128.0 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU alongside a 128 MB L3 cache. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or local storage disks, requiring external volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 450 GB/sec for uncached reads and 188 GB/sec for writes, alongside top-decile PassMark database throughput. Multi-core performance is robust across parallel compilation and compression tasks, though single-core compute operates at an average level. Lacking local storage overhead, the D32ps_v6 offers efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded web serving, distributed database nodes, code compilation pipelines, and containerized enterprise services.
